section_summary: This section records Japan’s late-1949 shift to a new foreign exchange and private export control system. It contains the concluding provisions of the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law, the proposed Foreign Exchange Control Board Establishment Law, detailed export procedures, and implementing orders. Despatches discuss the new system, while a telegram reports British sterling credits for trade with Japan.

subfiles.title: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law, concluding articles
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The concluding articles regulate services, exports and imports, appeals, enforcement, penalties, and the law’s commencement.
subfiles.summary: Articles 42–73 cover payments for services, movement of currency and securities, foreign trade permissions, administrative appeals and judicial review, inspection powers, and penalties. Supplementary provisions set an effective date no later than March 31, 1950, and repeal earlier exchange and trade measures.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Copy of Foreign Exchange Control Board Establishment Law
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a draft law establishing Japan’s Foreign Exchange Control Board.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the draft establishment law and relates it to the proposed foreign exchange and trade control law.

subfiles.title: Foreign Exchange Control Board Establishment Law
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The draft defines the board’s responsibilities, powers, membership, offices, and relationship with the Bank of Japan.
subfiles.summary: The board would manage the Foreign Exchange Special Account, monitor the exchange budget, keep transaction records, and advise on policy. The draft sets appointment and tenure rules, creates an executive office and Osaka branch, permits the Bank of Japan to handle board business, and penalizes disclosure of official secrets.

subfiles.title: British sterling credits for trade with Japan
subfiles.about: Three British banks are extending sterling credits to support imports from the sterling area.
subfiles.summary: Reports sterling trade credits, their distribution among banks, and the prospect of larger credits as two-way trade expands.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Memorandum on New Japanese Export Procedures
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAP guidance on export procedures effective December 5, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an export guidance memorandum pending a fuller analysis of Japan’s new laws and regulations.

subfiles.title: Information Memorandum No. 21: Exporting from Japan
subfiles.from: R. W. Hale, Foreign Trade and Commerce Division
subfiles.about: The memorandum introduces revised procedures for visible and invisible exports.
subfiles.summary: Supersedes six earlier guidance memoranda and attaches procedures effective December 5, 1949.

subfiles.title: Exporting from Japan
subfiles.from: Foreign Trade and Commerce Division, SCAP
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains bank, customs, licensing, payment, and remittance procedures for Japanese exports.
subfiles.summary: The guidance describes exchange rates, exporters’ retained foreign exchange, overseas agents, and the steps for bank certification and customs clearance. It also covers processing and compensatory deals, domestic sales, construction, military purchases, port services, and intangible transactions. Its annex lists goods requiring export licenses.

subfiles.title: New Japanese Foreign Exchange and Trade Controls with Special Reference to Institution of Private Export System
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch analyzes the new control law, its implementing measures, and Japan’s private export system.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reviews Law No. 228, the provisions effective December 1, and implementing orders on export licensing, exchange rates, banks, and the exchange budget. It explains the new private export process and designated banks. It also discusses Japanese efforts to prevent unfair competition and dumping in export trade.

subfiles.title: Statement on the new private export system
subfiles.about: The statement announces private export transactions and explains when licenses remain necessary.
subfiles.summary: Announces freer private export sales, foreign exchange bank handling, limited licensing, and exporters’ duty to respect destination-country competition laws.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order No. 375, concluding provisions (duplicate fragment)
subfiles.about: These pages repeat the concluding repeal and exchange-rate provisions of Cabinet Order No. 375.
subfiles.summary: Repeals portions of earlier controls and preserves specified exchange-rate references until amended.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order No. 375 Concerning the Date of Partial Enforcement of the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law
subfiles.about: The order identifies provisions of the new control law effective from December 1, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Brings exchange and export provisions into force, repeals related earlier measures, and provides temporary treatment for existing exchange-rate references.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order No. 377 Concerning Control of Export Trade
subfiles.about: The order establishes export licensing, bank certification, collection duties, exceptions, and controlled-goods lists.
subfiles.summary: The order requires licenses for listed goods, processing or compensatory deals, and nonstandard payment terms. It sets bank and customs certification procedures, requires collection of export proceeds, and allows review and sanctions for unfair practices. Attachments list controlled goods, exempt shipments, and personal property that certain travelers may take out of Japan.

subfiles.title: Export Trade Control Regulation
subfiles.from: Ministry of International Trade and Industry
subfiles.to: Exporters, foreign exchange banks, and customs
subfiles.about: The regulation specifies applications, contract terms, bank certification, reporting, and export declaration handling.
subfiles.summary: The regulation details how exporters apply for licenses and obtain approval for processing and compensatory contracts. It specifies documents for bank certification and requires reports on unpaid or subsequently collected export proceeds. It also directs how customs, banks, the ministry, and the Foreign Exchange Control Board handle declaration forms and invoices.
